assessment.mode: Provisional redesign candidate; generic learned-waiting novelty claim withdrawn

gate_evidence.G1: RealComm and the streaming studies document channel-related detection failures; Sinhala-specific early-decision failure remains unmeasured.
gate_evidence.G2: The question concerns a learned detector and when it has enough evidence to decide.
gate_evidence.G3: All three contributions train or adapt models rather than only call an API.
gate_evidence.G4: No suitable reusable Sinhala real/fake dataset with speaker and generator records has been secured.
gate_evidence.G5: The bounded study uses existing labels. New callers, recordings and expert labelling are excluded.
gate_evidence.G6: Learned stopping already exists in ALERT and EARLIEST. No specific Sinhala baseline failure or distinct repair has been demonstrated.
gate_evidence.G7: Training and comparison experiments are central; the app only demonstrates the result.
gate_evidence.G8: Metrics are defined, but suitable Sinhala data, source groups and clip lengths are not verified.
gate_evidence.G9: Data access and baseline reproduction must be resolved before the schedule is credible.
gate_evidence.G10: Section 6 gives separate questions, methods, comparisons and results for one shared problem.
gate_evidence.G11: The core uses selected audio and compact models; large-model training is optional.
gate_evidence.G12: Rights for the actual Sinhala fake audio and any generated derivatives remain unresolved.
gate_evidence.G13: Standard methods may suffice; waiting may not help; compression may damage early detection.

ratings.confidence_and_reason: High confidence in overlap: ALERT and EARLIEST already learn stopping; a distinct Sinhala contribution is unverified.
Low: Suitable reusable Sinhala human and generated speech has not been secured.
Low-medium: A bounded study is plausible once data and the first baseline work.
Medium: The plan trains adaptation, a waiting policy and a compact model.
Medium-low: Comparisons are defined, but suitable Sinhala test data and phone timings are missing.
Medium: Each member can test a separate idea against the same unchanged starting model.
Medium: Quick, reliable speech checks matter; protection during actual calls remains untested.
Medium-low: Small selected datasets and compact models should fit; resource use is not measured.
Medium: Existing audio can be replayed in small chunks without access to private calls.

scope: Controlled single-speaker human/generated clips replayed as prefixes; no partial-edit localisation or real-call protection claim.

claim_verdicts.claim: Telephone processing can seriously degrade speech-deepfake detection
claim_verdicts.limit: No Sinhala early-decision effect size established; RealComm is a recent unreplicated preprint.

claim_verdicts.claim: Learning a wait/decide policy from confidence and elapsed time is new
claim_verdicts.limit: Application to a different task can have research value, but the generic learning mechanism is established.

claim_verdicts.claim: Streaming efficient anti-spoofing under codec degradation is new
claim_verdicts.limit: These papers do not solve all Sinhala/method/phone issues; absence of a complete solution is not a novel contribution.

claim_verdicts.claim: Few labels or distribution change alone establishes an early-classification gap
claim_verdicts.limit: Adjacent general time-series protocols differ; task-specific failure and methodological addition remain to demonstrate.

claim_verdicts.claim: Known methods have a specific early-decision failure on Sinhala
claim_verdicts.limit: No source-controlled Sinhala prefix benchmark or experiment has been run.

claim_verdicts.claim: Synthetic derivatives make a Sinhala study possible
claim_verdicts.limit: Exact generator families, Sinhala output quality, licensing and leakage-safe provenance still need verification; a ready-made fake corpus is not required.

novelty_recheck.decision: Retain X33 as an unqualified redesign candidate, not a verified novel gap. Do not increase its score on the basis of corpus creation alone.
baseline_changes: ALERT or EARLIEST must be included alongside fixed-prefix and confidence-threshold baselines.
Padding and computation for each available prefix must be controlled; no full-clip feature leakage.
Compare errors, delay and coverage together on source/speaker/generator-separated data.
rejected_novelty_formulations: Few labels or drift alone as first early-classification setting
remaining_empirical_questions: Do established policies fail differently under separate Sinhala, generator and codec shifts after source controls?
If a failure is measured, is there an additional intervention beyond standard adaptation, calibration and learned stopping?
Would a documented Sinhala corpus and controlled benchmark meet the module's research-contribution standard?
limitations: Seven searches returned 130 occurrences and three duplication queries returned mixed-relevance leads; counts are not evidence of novelty.
One debate-map call returned an off-topic architecture-search item with no common ancestors; it is not evidence for this topic.
Recent zero-citation preprints were not penalised for citation count; older EARLIEST and RawSpectrogram records show continuing citations.
ALERT paper inspected at v1; metadata title reflects later wording. EARLIEST author PDF is a draft; DOI/title checked independently.
No models were trained, audio generated/downloaded or generator licences verified. Sinhala-specific gaps remain empirical hypotheses.
No new Markdown report created; X33 and its existing metadata are updated in place.
